clue.text: Non-combatant servant affected by disciple

parts.note: camp means affected, theatrically exaggerated
a disciple is a follower of a teacher

explanation.surface: A civilian helper is changed by coming under the influence of some devotee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' looks like a verb acting on the servant, but it is the adjective CAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically such people trailed an army as sutlers, cooks and attendants without bearing arms.

clue.text: Underground worker runs after dog

indicators.note: runs is placed behind the dog

parts.note: a collie is a sheepdog
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A miner jogs behind his dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal miner works below ground.

clue.text: Backchat from fly-by-night outside university?

indicators.note: one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a moth is an insect that flies at night

explanation.surface: Cheek from an untrustworthy operator just off campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent talk, cheek, as in giving someone lip.

clue.text: Shooting makes us deaf and sick at heart

indicators.note: the sick piece goes into the middle of the other letters
makes here means the letters of us deaf are made into something new

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: Gunfire deafens us and leaves us heartsick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges US DEAF to FUSADE, and 'at heart' puts ILL inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A volley of gunfire, many shots fired together.

clue.text: Van in which one would not find a 1 ac

definitions.text: Van in which one would not find a 1 ac

parts.words: Van in which one would not find a 1 ac
parts.note: van is the front of an army; 1 ac points to the 1-across answer, those civilian followers who trail at the rear

explanation.surface: A delivery lorry in which nobody would find a certain item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Van' suggests a vehicle, but it is the vanguard; camp followers bring up the rear, never the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The front position of an advancing army, the vanguard.

clue.text: Equivocal as Mrs. Malaprop's tongue

definitions.meaning: ambiguous like a prophecy from Delphi
Mrs Malaprop in Sheridan's The Rivals boasts of her '... tongue', meaning vernacular

explanation.definitionFit: Prophecies were famously ambiguous, and Sheridan's Mrs Malaprop misuses the word for vernacular.

clue.text: Not quite enough to make the GI drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of the GI staggering out of order

explanation.surface: An American soldier needs more than this many drinks to get tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is British slang for slightly drunk, so this number is just short of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom 'one over the eight' means tipsy, so that number of drinks falls just short.

clue.text: It's presented to people after a party

indicators.note: the people come behind the party

parts.note: a do is a party
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A gift handed to guests once a celebration is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift given to a charity or cause is presented to it.

clue.text: Odd characters in the hunt found a German

indicators.note: the first, third, fifth letters and so on are taken from the words that follow

explanation.surface: The hunt turned up a German among some strange people.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of an ancient Germanic people, used loosely for any German.

clue.text: State produces articles on Charlemagne's son

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: Charlemagne's son and successor was Louis I, the Pious
AN and A are both indefinite articles

explanation.surface: An American state is responsible for writing pieces about a Frankish emperor's heir.
explanation.walkthrough: The son is LOUIS I (Louis the Pious), with the numeral as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in the Deep South, named after the French king Louis XIV.

clue.text: Man dropped from tropical tree into a wood

indicators.note: the word man is taken away from the front of the tree's name

parts.note: a mangrove is a tropical tree of tidal swamps
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone falls out of a tropical tree into a wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A small group of trees, a copse.

clue.text: Trendy and vigorous way to relieve asthma

definitions.note: a verb defined by an action phrase: breathing in from an inhaler is the way relief comes

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
hale means healthy and vigorous

explanation.surface: Advice on a fashionable, energetic remedy for asthma sufferers.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma sufferers breathe medicine in from a puffer, the usual treatment.

clue.text: Prepare for publication a treatise to take away

parts.note: to sub is to subedit copy for printing
a tract is a treatise or pamphlet

explanation.surface: An editor is told to ready an essay for print and then remove it.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic, to deduct one number from another.

clue.text: A Whig, according to Johnson, giving old soldiers a pound

parts.note: RASC is the Royal Army Service Corps, a former British army corps
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Dr Johnson's opinion of a Whig politician who hands veterans a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Johnson, a staunch Tory, notoriously abused Whigs as scoundrels; the Whigs were a British political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson's low view of Whigs made them rogues and scoundrels, so a Whig in his book is a knave.

clue.text: Paper produced by firm in saint's island

indicators.note: the firm sits inside the saint's

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, so saint's is ST'S
CO is short for company, a firm
the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A newspaper published by a company on a holy man's island.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily newspaper published in Edinburgh.

clue.text: Boy following river could be from Llanelli

indicators.note: the boy's name comes after the river's name

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
Brian is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad walking behind a river might be Welsh.
explanation.walkthrough: Llanelli is a town in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambria is the Latin name for Wales, so the adjective means Welsh.

clue.text: Varsity athlete on marijuana in Kentucky?

parts.note: a Blue is a sportsman who has represented Oxford or Cambridge
grass is slang for marijuana

explanation.surface: A college sportsman on drugs in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is an Oxford or Cambridge sporting representative.
explanation.definitionFit: Kentucky's nickname is the Bluegrass State, after a meadow grass that grows there.

clue.text: Unusually pale side of seven stars

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of pale side come in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A pale side of an odd constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: The cluster in Taurus called the Seven Sisters.

clue.text: Tinker admits new novel is slipshod

indicators.note: one word lets the others inside it

parts.note: Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew

indicators.note: new signals the letters of novel made fresh in another order

explanation.surface: A handyman lets in a new book that is badly written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns NOVEL into OVENL, which goes inside SLY after its L.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean careless and untidy in work or appearance.

clue.text: Composed for engagement in Kent, possibly

parts.note: Kent is a county in the south-east of England, SE
a date is an appointment or engagement

explanation.surface: Music written for a wedding contract in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: The engagement is 'in' Kent in the sense of taking place there; the pieces simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and unruffled, like someone composed.

clue.text: Root for a trivial sum at the end of the act

indicators.note: the small sum is placed after the act

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act on stage
1p, one penny, read as the letters IP

explanation.surface: A penny for some vegetable at the end of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A root vegetable with white flesh.

clue.text: Airman's bird shown the back door

parts.note: PO is a Pilot Officer in the RAF, so the airman's is PO'S
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A pilot's bird is shown out by the rear entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear gate or side entrance, especially in a castle wall.

clue.text: Absent-minded girl's distinguishing feature

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so the girl's is Di's
a trait is a characteristic quality

explanation.surface: Being forgetful is this young woman's defining characteristic.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French, it means distracted and preoccupied.

clue.text: Frost, say, or Thomas of Erceldoune producing this

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: rime is hoarfrost

explanation.surface: Robert Frost or a medieval poet producing verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas of Erceldoune is Thomas the Rhymer, a Scottish poet and prophet; 'Frost' looks like the poet but is ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas the Rhymer was so called for the verses he made.

clue.text: Greek in old English ship — a monstrous person

indicators.note: one piece sits inside another

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A Greek aboard an ancient English vessel turns out to be a fiend.
explanation.definitionFit: A female ogre, a cruel and frightening woman.

clue.text: Uplifting holy books are an inspiration to poets

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplifting means the letters read upwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Inspiring scriptures motivate poets.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muse of lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: Tom loses little time in becoming a consumer

indicators.note: the little time drops away from the start of the tomcat

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, a mouser
mo is short for moment

explanation.surface: A man wastes little time becoming a shopper.
explanation.definitionFit: One who uses up goods, a customer.

clue.text: In "Rigoletto". a dyed-in-the-wood sycophant

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: In Verdi's opera there is a thoroughgoing flatterer.
explanation.walkthrough: The dot after the opera's title is the page's comma.
explanation.definitionFit: A fawning hanger-on who flatters the powerful.

clue.text: Paid rates irregularly, being different

indicators.note: irregularly suggests the letters set out in no fixed order

explanation.surface: Someone paid their local taxes at uneven intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: Essentially unlike, not able to be compared.

clue.text: The obvious utensil, might one say, to go with the nursery dish?

definitions.text: The obvious utensil, might one say, to go with the nursery dish?

parts.words: The obvious utensil, might one say, to go with the nursery dish?
parts.note: a nursery pudding course calls for a spoon named after that very course

explanation.surface: A nanny asks which piece of cutlery naturally suits a child's pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium spoon between teaspoon and tablespoon, used for puddings.
